c.tagline: Indonesia's sprawling capital of malls, markets, and endless motorbikes.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird is the trusted metered taxi brand; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front pricing. Avoid unmarked touts at the airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing and traffic-jam phone-snatching; caution at demonstrations — use Grab/Gojek.

hood_desc: A leafy, upscale colonial-era district of tree-lined streets, embassies, and museums; central and calm, it suits travelers who want green surroundings within reach of the center.
South Jakarta's expat-favored district packed with bars, cafes, restaurants, and boutiques; the go-to area for nightlife and international dining.
The historic Dutch colonial old town (Kota Tua) around Fatahillah Square, with cobblestone plazas, museums, and the Sunda Kelapa harbor; the city's main sightseeing quarter.
The Sudirman Central Business District, a cluster of gleaming skyscrapers, luxury malls, rooftop bars, and high-end hotels; a modern base for business travelers and upscale nightlife.
The central Thamrin corridor around the Bundaran HI roundabout and Grand Indonesia mall, lined with flagship hotels and transit links; the most convenient walkable base for first-timers.
lodging: The Hermitage, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel

water.note: Stick to bottled or purified water; even locals avoid tap water in Jakarta.

transit.hours: MRT and TransJakarta run roughly 5:00 AM to midnight; the KRL Commuterline runs from around 4:00 AM to midnight. No 24-hour rail service, so ride-hailing fills the late-night gap.
transit.note: Jakarta's rail backbone is the MRT (north-south line), supplemented by the extensive TransJakarta BRT busway network, the KRL Commuterline serving Greater Jakarta (Jabodetabek), and the newer Jakarta LRT and Jabodebek LRT lines.
transit.pay: Most systems use the tap-in JakLingko card or bank e-money cards (as of 2026 the MRT and TransJakarta also accept the JakLingko app and QRIS). Fares are cheap (TransJakarta ~3,500 IDR flat; MRT distance-based).

bus: Intercity buses from Kampung Rambutan, Pulo Gebang, and Kalideres terminals
ferry: Ferries to the Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu) from Ancol Marina and Muara Angke
train: Intercity trains from Gambir and Pasar Senen stations to Bandung, Yogyakarta, and Surabaya

transit.m: Railink airport train to BNI City / Sudirman (~40-55 min)
Damri airport bus to points around the city (~60-90 min)
Blue Bird metered taxi to city center (45-90 min in traffic)

tip.r: Not expected; many restaurants already add a 5-10% service charge. Rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.
